title: 长寿金鱼与一睡三年的蜗牛
pdf: https://michael-podcast-1513696684.cos.ap-chengdu.myqcloud.com/vol27/Vol27_晚读讲义_长寿金鱼与一睡三年的蜗牛_v1.pdf
pdfName: Vol27_晚读讲义_长寿金鱼与一睡三年的蜗牛_v1.pdf

blocks.en: Hello, young explorers, and welcome back to Michael's Morning Listening! Today we meet two slow champions: a little goldfish that outlived most dogs, and a snail that can sleep for years. One teaches us patience; the other, the art of waiting. Let's go!
blocks.title: 开场白
blocks.cn: 你好，小小探险家们，欢迎回到 Michael 的早听晚读！今天我们要认识两位“慢冠军”：一条活得比大多数狗狗还久的小金鱼，和一只一睡就能睡好几年的蜗牛。一个教我们耐心，一个教我们等待的艺术。出发吧！

blocks.en: Most goldfish live ten to fifteen years. But one little goldfish named Tish lived forty-three years — a world record! A seven-year-old boy named Peter won him at a fair, in a roll-a-coin game. Peter's mother Hilda then looked after Tish for most of his long life. His vivid orange scales slowly turned silver, like an old man's hair.
blocks.title: 长寿金鱼蒂什
blocks.cn: 大多数金鱼能活十到十五年。可有一条名叫蒂什的小金鱼，活了四十三年——创了世界纪录！七岁的男孩彼得在一个集市上玩滚硬币的游戏，把它赢回了家。之后，彼得的妈妈希尔达照顾了蒂什漫长一生中的大部分时光。他鲜艳的橙色鳞片慢慢变成了银色，就像老爷爷的白头发。

blocks.en: The caption under his photo, on a page of the record book, says he lived in a simple bowl, with fresh water and quiet days. He even survived a great escape: one day he jumped out of his bowl, but Hilda found him in time, and he swam away as if nothing had happened. The record book makes no discrimination between big animals and small ones — a tiny fish can be a champion too.
blocks.title: 长寿金鱼蒂什
blocks.cn: 纪录书里他照片下面的说明写着：他住在一个简单的鱼缸里，有干净的水和安静的日子。他甚至经历过一次大逃亡：有一天他从鱼缸里跳了出来，不过希尔达及时发现了他，他又像什么都没发生一样游走了。纪录书不分大动物还是小动物——一条小小的鱼也可以成为冠军。

blocks.en: Tish was not alone. A cat named Creme Puff lived thirty-eight years — longer than most dogs! Tish's story appeared in every format: in books, in newspapers, and on television. Tish became an ambassador for all small pets: with patience and care, even the smallest friend can stay a very long time.
blocks.title: 长寿金鱼蒂什
blocks.cn: 在纪录书里，蒂什并不孤单。一只名叫“奶油泡芙”的猫活了三十八年——比大多数狗狗还久！蒂什的故事以各种形式出现过：书里、报纸上、电视上都有。他成了所有小宠物的代言人：只要有耐心和细心的照顾，即使是最小的朋友，也能陪伴我们很久很久。

blocks.en: Now meet a slower champion: the garden snail. On a warm day, a snail slides along a leaf, leaving a silver trail. But when hot, dry days come and the garden dries up, the snail does something amazing. It climbs into its shell and seals the door with a layer of dried slime, like closing a little gate. Inside, its body slows almost to a stop. It does not eat. It does not move. It waits.
blocks.title: 一睡三年的蜗牛
blocks.cn: 现在认识一位更慢的冠军：花园蜗牛。温暖的日子里，蜗牛沿着叶子慢慢爬，留下一道银色的痕迹。可当炎热干燥的日子到来、花园干透时，蜗牛会做出一件了不起的事。它缩进壳里，用一层干掉的黏液封住门口，就像关上一扇小门。在壳里，它的身体几乎慢到停了下来。它不吃东西，也不动弹，只是等着。

blocks.en: This deep sleep is not really sleep. Scientists call it estivation — a summer sleep for dry times. In this state, a snail can wait for months. In the driest places, some snails have waited for years — up to three years! A pedestrian may walk right past the quiet shell at the bottom of the garden wall. The snail is deaf to the footsteps and the wind, but it feels the change in the air.
blocks.title: 一睡三年的蜗牛
blocks.cn: 这种深沉的睡眠其实根本不是真正的睡眠。科学家叫它“夏眠”——为了熬过干旱的夏天而睡。在这种状态下，蜗牛可以等上好几个月。在最干旱的地方，有些蜗牛甚至等了好几年——长达三年！路过的行人可能从花园墙根那只安静的壳边走过，却从没注意到它。蜗牛听不见脚步声和风声，但它能感觉到空气的变化。

blocks.en: Then, at last, the rain comes. A fine spray falls on the garden. The snail wakes, opens its little gate, and slides out into the morning light. The sun rises in the east, and the garden comes alive again.
blocks.title: 一睡三年的蜗牛
blocks.cn: 终于，雨来了。细细的水花洒落在花园里。蜗牛醒了，打开它的小门，慢慢爬进晨光里。太阳从东方升起，花园又活了过来。

blocks.en: Here's today's idiom: 'saved by the bell.' In a boxing match, when a tired boxer is almost beaten, the bell rings to end the round — and he is saved by the bell! We use it when something saves us at the very last moment. Here's an example: 'Leo forgot his lines in the school play, but he was saved by the bell when the lunch bell rang and everyone erupted in cheers.' When were you saved by the bell?
blocks.title: 今日俚语
blocks.cn: 今天的俚语是“saved by the bell”（被铃声救了）。在拳击比赛中，拳手累得快要输掉的时候，铃声响起，一回合结束了——拳手就被铃声救了！我们用这个说法来形容在最后一刻被什么事情从麻烦里救出来。举个例子：“利奥在学校的话剧里忘了台词，可午餐铃一响，大家欢呼起来，他就被铃声救了。”你有过被铃声救了的时候吗？

blocks.en: Let's think about our stories. Tish lived forty-three years, and a snail can wait three years for rain. Now, two questions for you. First: if you had a pet, what would you do to help it live a long, happy life? Second: if you could sleep for three years, what would you most want to see when you wake up? Talk about it with your family!
blocks.title: 结束语与互动问题
blocks.cn: 我们来想想今天的故事。蒂什活了四十三年，蜗牛可以等三年才等来一场雨。现在，轮到回答两个问题。第一：如果你养了一只宠物，你会怎么做，才能让它活得又久又开心？第二：如果你能一睡三年，醒来时最想看到什么？和家人聊聊吧！

blocks.en: That's all for today, young explorers. Be patient like Tish, and brave like a snail. And remember: sometimes help comes just in time — saved by the bell! See you tomorrow morning!
blocks.title: 告别
blocks.cn: 今天的节目就到这里啦，小小探险家们。像蒂什一样有耐心，像蜗牛一样勇敢。还要记住：有时候，帮助会在刚刚好的时候到来——被铃声救了！明天早上见！

children.text: at the bottom of the garden wall
情态动词 + 动词原形
：may 后面跟动词原形 walk，不加 s、不加 to。may 在这里表示“可能”，不是“一定”——行人可能走过，也可能停下来看。
里的 right 不是“右”，而是“径直、直接”：walk right past = 径直走过，连看都没看一眼。这个 right 是副词，给 walk 加了“头也不回”的味道。
at the bottom of the garden wall
：at the bottom of（在……的底部）告诉我们壳在哪里——花园墙的根部。介词短语放在名词后面，专门交代位置。
：quiet（安静的）放在名词 shell 前面，说明这只壳一声不响。英语里形容词一般都站在它修饰的名词前面。
人物（行人）→ 可能的动作（径直走过）→ 对象（安静的壳）→ 位置（花园墙根）
。一句话里藏着情态动词、副词、介词短语和形容词四个机关。
. When the garden dries up, the snail
"climbs into its shell and seals the door with a layer of dried slime."
"We use it when something saves us at the very last moment."
"Scientists call it estivation — a summer sleep for dry times."
D. Your own translations — there is no key for this part. Read your Chinese aloud and check that it sounds natural.
